subject: Project Idea and hope for feedback

messages.author: d65ba03cb57bb5b5
messages.subject: Project Idea and hope for feedback
parts:
Hi List,

I have a project idea and I am wondering if anyone would be willing/interested
to serve as a mentor.

As a big fan of R and IE/OR student , I've used many of R's related package in several course projects in engineering economics and finance in the past year. However, many non-statistics professors whom I came across still  think that R and its packages are not up-to par with other similar open source/commercial software that are used in quantitative finance due in part of a lack of comprehensive and standard functions, utilities and framework.

I'm interested to use SOC 2010 to help to do the following:

1) extend Rquantlib to interface with ISDA  open source standard model (written in c,is it possible to use Rcpp for this?)
http://www.cdsmodel.com/cdsmodel/documentation.page?#

2) continue to extend Rquantlib to include more wrapper functions to quantlib including but not limited to the library involved with stochastic processes and Monte Carlo framework

3) continue to find way to take advantage of R's handling in statistical simulation and graphical utility to visualize analysis results.

I'm not sure if these are good ideas to proceed. Does anyone think it would be useful to R users and the  community in general ?   if you have any feedback , please let me know.

thanks,
-Nelson

RQuantLib is one of my packages, and was a (successful) GSoC 2009 project.
However, I did not list it for 2010 and I do not believe that I will have
time to mentor it this year.

You are of course more than welcome to work on RQuantLib outside of GSoC.
Khanh and I would very much welcome contributions along the lines of 1), 2)
and 3) and invite to come to the rquantlib-devel mailing list.

But for GSoC 2010, unless someone else wants to mentor (or you manage to make
me change my mind, but I already have two other proposals out and am admin
here this year), this may not be an option.

Sorry to be a bearer of bad news here.

Regards, Dirk
